title: Internal Brief: Magnetic Fusion Pilots
content: Internal research note: tokamak and stellarator pilots have demonstrated higher plasma confinement times. Commercial plants still require advances in blanket materials, remote maintenance, and tritium breeding ratios above 1.0. Estimated earliest grid-connected pilots remain in the 2030s under optimistic funding scenarios.

title: Internal Brief: Fusion Economics
content: Cost models inside the KB suggest levelized cost of electricity for first-of-a-kind fusion plants may exceed advanced fission and renewables-plus-storage unless high capacity factors and long component lifetimes are achieved. Supply chain for high-temperature superconductors is a bottleneck.

title: Internal Brief: Regulatory Path
content: Licensing frameworks for fusion differ from fission in several jurisdictions. Internal analysis notes that clearer regulatory pathways reduce investor uncertainty but do not remove materials and fuel-cycle risks.

title: Internal Brief: Clean Energy Portfolio
content: Fusion is treated as a long-horizon option in the internal energy portfolio. Near-term decarbonization still relies on renewables, storage, efficiency, and existing firm low-carbon sources.
